title: Dimension-lowering preparation of complete local marked log regular models
statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Assume $U(V,W)$ from [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology] for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $V$ of Krull dimension at most $d-1$ and every nowhere dense closed subset $W\subset V$. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A$ is a nonzero normal complete Noetherian local domain of dimension $d$, and let $Z\subset X$ be nowhere dense closed. There is a finite ordinary alteration covering $(h_a:M_a\to X)_a$ with each $M_a$ nonempty integral excellent Noetherian, and nowhere dense closed subsets $B_a\subset M_a$ such that $(M_a,B_a)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. For every $a$ there is an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_a\subset\mathcal O_{M_a}$ whose zero-set is $h_a^{-1}(Z)$ and is contained in $B_a$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The unit ideal is permitted when $Z$ is empty. In particular the output sources are log regular; regularity of these sources is not asserted.

Schemes, integral schemes, excellence, Noetherianness, normal rings, completion and Krull dimension mean [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose VII 3.1--4.2, pp.81--82, stopping before the log resolution theorem 4.3: V 3.1.3--3.1.4, p.66 (partial algebraization); regular completion pullback in VII 3.2; compactification and Cartierization in 3.3; ordinary marked nodal alteration in 3.4; lower-dimensional uniformization of the base in 4.1; VI 1.9 in 4.2. The Cartier ideal is the pulled-back ideal after the blowup in 3.3; no assertion of regular models is included.

proof.text: The residue field of $A$ has characteristic $0$ or a single prime $p$. Choose a prime $\ell$ different from that characteristic; its image in $A$ is a unit. This is only an auxiliary parameter: we impose no degree restriction on the output. By [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], $X$ is excellent. Apply [lem-per-prime-to-ell-marked-algebraization] to $(X,Z)$: obtain $p:X^+\to X$, the regular completion morphism $g:X^+\to W$, and $W\to Y_0$ with $Y_0$ affine excellent regular of dimension $d-1$ and generic fibre an integral curve. Write $Z_W$ for its marking, so $p^{-1}Z=g^{-1}Z_W$. This uses ordinary completion, not strict henselization. The generic fibre of $Z_W$ is nowhere dense in the integral generic curve (it misses its generic point), hence has dimension at most zero by [lem-pc-nowhere-dense-dim-zero].

Apply [lem-per-proper-generic-curve-preparation] to $W\to Y_0$ and $Z_W$, with the chosen $\ell$. It gives an affine integral excellent $Y_1$ with $\dim Y_1\le d-1$, a proper $P\to Y_1$ with smooth geometrically integral generic curve, an effective Cartier divisor $E$ with finite etale generic fibre, and a dense open $P^\circ\subset P$ with a proper surjective generically finite map $h:P^\circ\to W$ satisfying $|E|\cap P^\circ=h^{-1}Z_W$. In the ordinary topology $h$ is a singleton cover, regardless of its generic degree. In particular Cartierization has happened before the subsequent nodal alterations.

source.place: VII 3.3, p.82 (compactification and blowing up the marking); the existing preparation also supplies the generic smooth and etale hypotheses needed in 3.4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-marked-nodal-reduction] to $P\to Y_1$ with the Cartier marking $E$. Its base hypothesis holds: $Y_1$ is affine Noetherian, hence projective over its own affine spectrum via the identity. Obtain alterations $a:C\to P$, $b:Y'\to Y_1$, a projective flat finitely presented nodal curve $f:C\to Y'$, and $D,T$ as in that lemma: $D$ is finite etale over $Y'$, lies in the smooth locus, $f$ is smooth off $T$, and $a^{-1}|E|\subseteq |D|\cup f^{-1}T$. The base $Y'$ is integral excellent Noetherian. Since $b$ is proper dominant generically finite, [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension] gives $\dim Y'=\dim Y_1\le d-1$.

The induction hypothesis applies to the reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $Y'$ and nowhere dense $T$. Choose its finite ordinary alteration cover $(S_j\to Y')_j$ with integral regular sources and inverse images $T_j$ strict normal crossings boundaries, as specified by $U$ in [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. These $S_j$ are excellent: their maps are finite type and $Y'$ is excellent, so apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] on affine charts. By [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart], every $(S_j,T_j)$ is log regular. This is the only use of the induction assumption; no uniformization theorem in dimension $d$ is invoked.

Put $C_j=C\times_{Y'}S_j$, with marking $D_j$ and morphism $f_j:C_j\to S_j$. The nodal base-change statement [lem-trf-projective-nodal-family-geometry] supplies projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, the geometric fibres and the pulled-back smooth locus. Etaleness of $D_j\to S_j$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; the original $D$ is relative effective Cartier because it is Cartier and $D\to Y\prime$ is flat (etale). Thus [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier] and [lem-pc-recd-pullback] give the Cartier property of $D_j$ under this arbitrary base change. Thus [lem-trf-nodal-log-regularity] applies, giving the log regular pair $(C_j,B_j)$ with $B_j=|D_j|\cup f_j^{-1}T_j$. Since $f$ is flat with geometrically reduced fibres, [lem-per-ordinary-alteration-cover-base-change] says the usual products $C_j\to C$ are ordinary alteration objects and form a finite covering. In particular all their generic points map to the generic point of $C$.

By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], all local rings of $C_j$ are normal domains. Pull the ideal of $E$ back along $C_j\to C\to P$. A local nonzero generator stays nonzero on every component because the generic points map to the generic points of the integral schemes $C$ and $P$; in each local domain it is a non-zero-divisor. Hence this is an effective Cartier ideal by [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Its zero-set is contained in $B_j$, by the marked nodal containment. Restrict to $C_j^\circ=C_j\times_PP^\circ$. The pair stays log regular under this open restriction by [lem-per-log-regular-pair-regular-pullback]. Its Cartier ideal now has zero-set equal to the inverse image of $Z_W$. The finite cover $C_j\to C$ restricts to a cover of $C\times_PP^\circ$ by the ordinary base-change lemma. Compose it with the proper alteration $C\times_PP^\circ\to P^\circ$ and $h:P^\circ\to W$: covering-sieve transitivity in [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology] gives a finite covering $C_j^\circ\to W$.

source.place: VII 3.3--4.2, p.82, retaining the Cartier ideal from 3.3; II 2.3.1--2.3.4, p.28.

proof.text: Base change the last cover by the regular completion morphism $g:X^+\to W$. The ordinary base-change lemma gives a finite cover $N_j=C_j^\circ\times_WX^+\to X^+$. Its projection to $C_j^\circ$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change], since $C_j^\circ\to W$ is finite type. Apply [lem-per-log-regular-pair-regular-pullback] to obtain log regular pairs $(N_j,B'_j)$. Flat pullback preserves their Cartier markings by [lem-pc-flat-pullback-effective-cartier-ideal]; their zero-sets are precisely the inverse images of $p^{-1}Z$, and lie in $B'_j$. The sources are Noetherian and excellent: $N_j\to X^+$ is finite type, $X^+$ is complete Noetherian local, and [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] apply.

source.place: VII 3.2, p.82, applied to the log regular models of 4.2; Stacks Tag 07C1 (more-algebra-lemma-regular-base-change), Tag 02OO (divisors-lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined).

proof.text: Log regularity makes each $N_j$ normal by [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure]. By [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] it is a finite disjoint union of nonempty open and closed integral components. Take these as $M_a$, discarding empty sources. The ordinary component-cover statement and covering-sieve transitivity show that the $M_a$ still cover $X^+$. Open restriction retains log regularity, the nowhere dense boundary and the Cartier ideal. Finally $p:X^+\to X$ is finite surjective and generically finite, so is an ordinary singleton cover. Compose with it to obtain the required finite cover of $X$. All markings have zero-set exactly $h_a^{-1}Z$ by the two earlier inverse-image equalities. If $Z$ is empty choose the unit ideal; it is generated by $1$ and has empty zero-set. No step applies log resolution or asserts that a log regular source is regular.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q99-dd0165d69 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the 8-step ILO VII 3.1–4.2 split in full against ILO VII pp.81–83 and V 3.1.1–3.1.4 (p.66) and against every cited node statement; it is sound. The item statement is unchanged (byte-equal to live), and the proof stops before Kato 4.3, so the sources are log regular, not regular. Step checks: (1) a prime ℓ different from the residue characteristic is a unit in the local ring; the generic fibre of Z_W misses the generic point of W, so dim ≤ 0. (2) Every curve-preparation hypothesis comes from step 1, and h is a proper surjective alt singleton. (3) Y₁ affine is projective over itself (N=0); closed-dominant-dimension gives dim Y′ ≤ d−1. (4) Induction applies to the integral excellent Y′; the S_j are excellent by finite-type-localization. (5) D is finite étale, hence flat, hence relative Cartier, so recd-pullback applies; f_j is smooth off T_j because U ⊇ f⁻¹(Y′∖T); every nodal-log-regularity hypothesis holds. (6) The Cartier generator stays nonzero in the normal local domains because generic points map to η_C and C→P is dominant; the zero set lies in B_j; moving covers from alt/T to alt/W is an elementary slice argument. (7) g is regular, hence geometrically reduced; regular-base-change is applied on affine charts. (8) Clopen integral components plus the finite surjective p; empty Z handled. New nodes: (a) ordinary-alteration-cover-base-change is true: flatness lifts generic points, the fibre over a generic t is finite free over S′_η, generators are stable under base change, and the component clause holds via ⊔R_i; it does not duplicate the ℓ′ versions. Advisory B3: its 'nodal curve morphism' has no bracket, though def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres is in its stmt_deps. (b) log-regular-pair-regular-pullback is true: C/IC is flat over regular A/I with regular fibre (00OF/031E), and the 00ON dimension formulas leave the rank unchanged. It is not a log-smooth or SNC duplicate, and neither new node restates the item. Dropped-route finding: BFS in side-live shows the item is reached via qe-weak-uniformization ← … ← gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification ← lem-sfb-field-log-smooth-gabber-modification ← … ← thm-weil-final-rh. That is the same sfb-revived branch as the PASSed parent Q147, so I judged it on merits. complete-local-excellence and regular-boundary-divisorial-chart are already reached (0 nodes added). proper-generic-curve-preparation adds only itself. prime-to-ell-marked-algebraization adds 38 dropped nodes (equivariant Cohen–Gabber and Elkik/rig-étale); I accepted this because VII 3.1 itself uses V 3.1.3, which is the prime-to-ℓ theorem, no ordinary node exists, and an ordinary twin would be a C5 duplicate. MAINTAINER NOTE: landing this revives that 38-node chain into the Weil closure. If that is unwanted, the route decision for the whole sfb→gabber-absolute branch needs escalation; no fix to this item avoids it. The artin-gabber repair-note ban covers that node and its three children, not this sfb-reached item. Batch 5: every flagged trf/exc node is already in the nt-target-weil/zeta closure without this item. All are generic algebra, dimension or log-geometry tools or definitions, and none is the trace formula or Poincaré duality statement; tool_uses accepted. Details are in review.md.
